Concept

Hear it. Understand it. Remember it.

Who it’s for
People who find spoken information difficult to process or retain, including some people with ADHD, auditory processing differences, and hearing difficulties.
The goal
Turn a conversation into something the person can revisit, clarify, and act on at their own pace.
Intended workflowPlanned capabilitiesQuestionsShare feedback

THE EVERYDAY CHALLENGE

ClearCue starts
with a real need.

Hearing a sentence, understanding its meaning, and remembering what to do next are different demands. Instructions can be lost when a conversation moves faster than someone can process it.

Turn a conversation into something the person can revisit, clarify, and act on at their own pace.

HOW IT COULD WORK

A thoughtful path
through the moment.

This walkthrough illustrates the intended experience. It describes the product direction, not functionality available on this website.

  1. Start with clear consent

    The planned experience would make recording state visible and provide start, pause, and stop controls. Consent and privacy requirements would shape the capture process.

  2. Recover the thread

    Review a transcript or a brief recap of what was missed. Keep a path back to the relevant passage instead of relying only on an AI summary.

  3. Clarify before acting

    Separate instructions, commitments, and open questions. A user could review a suggested follow-up question when a detail is uncertain.

PLANNED CAPABILITIES

The details
we’re exploring.

  • Provide real-time transcription and accessible conversation summaries.
  • Identify instructions, commitments, and important details.
  • Offer a “What did I miss?” review of recent conversation.
  • Turn complex verbal instructions into manageable steps.
  • Make confusing passages easier to revisit and clarify.
  • Suggest follow-up questions and optional visual reminders.

AN EVERYDAY EXAMPLE

What support could look like.

After an appointment, someone could review a concise summary, find the next steps, and see which instructions need clarification with the provider.

A design consideration

Recording would require appropriate consent and clear controls. Transcripts and summaries can be wrong; important details should be checked against the conversation.

ACCESSIBILITY & CONTROL

Designed around
the person using it.

Readable live text, concise recaps, adjustable presentation, and discreet optional reminders would focus on comprehension and follow-through.

Privacy, affordability, and user autonomy are shared Biro.dev design principles. Product-specific data practices, supported access methods, and any offline capabilities would be explained before public release.

Read our design commitments

QUESTIONS ABOUT CLEARCUE

A clearer picture.

Would ClearCue record in the background?

Background recording is not a promised feature. The product direction centers on visible recording controls and appropriate consent.

Would it replace hearing support or an interpreter?

No replacement is claimed. ClearCue is a concept for reviewing and understanding speech, with limitations that would need to be evaluated before release.

Would conversations be processed on the device?

The processing model is still being defined. Local and cloud processing choices, retention, and deletion would be explained before people use the product.

When can I use ClearCue?

ClearCue is in early concept development. There is no public release date, price, or supported-platform list yet. The next step is to develop and evaluate the intended experience.
